mechanism_narrative: The continued decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates fewer commuting trips, which suppresses incidental retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC moving lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below their t-3w levels.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES stays depressed, more time is spent at home and discretionary shopping is displaced, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 10 and WORKPLACES below -10 for one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 10 and WORKPLACES is below -10.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduces foot traffic near malls and dining areas, and the combined shock lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks more than either series alone.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are below -20 and moving down together.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls another 5 points from its current level, that threshold implies a renewed mobility clampdown that cuts shopping trips and drives RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls 5 points below the current week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already at -27.0 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the next 7 days after TRANSIT drops at least 5 points below the current week.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM alongside falling RETAIL_REC signals substitution toward essential trips and away from discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC continues to weaken over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 15.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS usually absorbs leisure time that would otherwise go to malls and restaurants, so higher PARKS mobility should reduce RETAIL_REC with a four-week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -15 after being below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform the prior 28-day mean in the four weeks after PARKS crosses above -15 from below -20.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated into the year-end period, holiday stock-up behavior crowds out discretionary retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 20 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is 19.4 in t-0w after 26.1 in t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean despite GROCERY_PHARM staying above 20 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both keep falling while RESIDENTIAL keeps rising, the policy environment is tightening enough to suppress mixed-purpose trips and push RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
